q: Which law is the Subdivision and Condominium Buyers Protective Decree?
n: PD 957 governs subdivisions and condominiums. BP 220 covers economic and socialized housing, the cheaper tier below it.

q: Under RA 9514, what is the longest dead-end aisle allowed in a seating area?
n: 6.1 m. Past that an occupant would have to walk back into the fire to escape.

q: How should street lighting be spaced where poles stand 50 m apart?
n: One lamp on every pole at 50 m spacing. Closer than 50 m, every other pole is enough.

q: Which law is the National Building Code of the Philippines?
n: PD 1096, in force since 1977, with its Revised IRR of 2004.

q: What clear distance must separate seats placed back to back?
n: 1.00 m back to back, so two rows can pass without touching.

q: In economic and socialized housing, what septic tank arrangement is allowed?
n: Communal or individual, per PD 856. Open market and medium cost housing must give each unit its own.

q: Which seating condition allows the most seats between aisles, at 15?
n: Open air without a backrest. Nothing overhead to trap smoke and nothing to climb over.

q: Under RA 9514, what aisle width serves more than 60 seats?
n: 915 mm for more than 60 seats, 760 mm for 60 or fewer.

q: Where must the minimum drainage system be laid?
n: Underground, so the road surface stays usable and open water does not stand.

q: What two parts make up the required water tank capacity?
n: 20% of average daily demand plus a fire reserve. Daily demand itself is 150 litres per person per day.

q: Under PD 1096, what standard spacing applies between seat backs in successive rows?
n: 840 mm back to back. RA 9514 is slightly tighter at 830 mm.

q: How may garbage collection be arranged in a subdivision?
n: Independently, or through the local government unit.

q: PD 957 sets a minimum drainage pipe diameter of 300 mm. What is that in metres?
n: 0.30 m. Anything narrower silts up and floods the road.

q: In continental seating, what spacing applies to a row of up to 35 seats?
n: 500 mm. It grows with the row: 450 mm to 18 seats, 500 mm to 35, 525 mm to 45, 550 mm beyond.

q: Which vehicle uses a 3.00 x 9.00 m parking slot?
n: A jeepney or shuttle. A standard truck or bus needs 3.60 x 12.00 m, an articulated truck 3.60 x 18.00 m.

q: Under PD 1096, what parking slot size serves a standard truck or bus?
n: 3.60 x 12.00 m. Stretch it to 18.00 m long for an articulated truck.

q: What is the minimum seat width in continental seating?
n: 450 mm minimum, 480 mm maximum.

q: Under RA 9514, how does aisle width change once a row exceeds 60 seats?
n: It steps up from 760 mm to 915 mm. More seats means more people funnelling into that aisle.

q: Under PD 957, what parking slot size applies to perpendicular or diagonal parking in open market housing?
n: 2.50 x 5.00 m, the standard car slot. Parallel parking needs a longer, narrower 2.00 x 6.00 m.

q: Under PD 1096, what row spacing applies to seats with a backrest?
n: 750 mm with a backrest, 600 mm without. A backrest takes depth the row must give up.

q: In continental seating, how does row spacing grow as the seat count rises?
n: 450 mm, then 500, 525 and 550 mm. The longer the row, the more room each person needs to shuffle past.

q: Under BP 220, how many living units in a multi-family dwelling or condominium share one parking slot?
n: One slot per 8 living units. Economic and socialized housing pools parking, unlike PD 1096 which gives a slot per unit on large lots.

q: Under RA 9514, what is the maximum row spacing in a seating area?
n: 830 mm maximum, 680 mm minimum.

q: Which water figure is a daily demand rather than a tank sizing factor?
n: 150 litres per person per day is the demand. The tank is sized at 20% of that demand plus a fire reserve.

q: For low-income single-detached units on 100 sq m lots, what pooled parking rate applies?
n: One slot per 10 units. Pooled parking keeps the cost of a socialized subdivision down.

q: How many seats may sit between a wall and an aisle?
n: 7 between a wall and an aisle, 14 between two aisles. A wall traps you, so the run is halved.

q: Which drainage system goes with open market and medium cost housing?
o: Open market/medium cost - open earth canal
n: Reinforced concrete pipes. Economic and socialized housing may instead use a concrete-lined canal with a load-bearing cover.

q: Under PD 1096, what parking ratio applies to a residential unit on a lot above 100 sq m?
n: One slot per unit. It thins out as lots shrink: one per 4 units at 50 to 100 sq m, one per 8 below 50 sq m.

q: What is the maximum number of seats between aisles for open-air seating without a backrest?
n: 15. Open air with no backrest is the loosest case, because escape is easy and rows are shallow.

q: Which law is the Accessibility Law?
n: BP 344, the Accessibility Law of 1983. Its current rules are the 2024 Revised IRR.

q: Under PD 1096, what width must an aisle have when it serves seats on both sides?
n: 1.00 m serving both sides, 800 mm serving one side only.

q: What average daily water demand is used for subdivision housing?
n: 150 litres per person per day, written as 150 LCPD.

q: Which fire code was repealed by RA 9514?
n: PD 1185, the Fire Code of 1977. RA 9514 replaced it in 2008, and its current rules are the 2019 Revised IRR.

q: How many rows of seats does each required pair of exit doors serve?
n: One pair of exit doors per 5 rows, each pair 1.70 m wide.

q: How should street lighting be spaced where poles stand less than 50 m apart?
n: Every other pole. Poles set closer than 50 m would otherwise over-light the road.

q: Under PD 1096, what rise is provided between successive seating rows?
n: 400 mm of rise per row, enough to see over the head in front.

q: Under PD 1096, what is the maximum slope of a seating aisle?
n: 1:8, that is 12.5%. Steeper than that and an audience leaving in the dark starts to stumble.

q: What minimum drainage pipe diameter applies in PD 957 housing?
n: 300 mm. Anything narrower silts up and floods the road.

q: Which two seating conditions are limited to 6 seats between aisles?
n: Within a building without a backrest, and open air with a backrest. Both sit between the 7-seat wall case and the 15-seat open-air case.

q: Under RA 9514, what aisle width serves 60 seats or fewer?
n: 760 mm for 60 or fewer, rising to 915 mm above that.

q: What minimum drainage system is required for open market and medium cost housing?
n: Reinforced concrete pipes, laid underground.

q: Below what pole spacing does street lighting drop to every other pole?
n: Below 50 m. At 50 m and beyond, every pole carries a lamp.

q: Under RA 9514, what standard spacing applies between seat backs in successive rows?
n: 830 mm, marginally tighter than the 840 mm PD 1096 uses.

q: Under PD 1096, what is the longest parking slot provided for any vehicle?
n: 18.00 m, for an articulated truck. A standard truck or bus takes 12.00 m, a jeepney 9.00 m.

q: Under PD 1096, what is the standard parking slot size for perpendicular or diagonal parking?
n: 2.50 x 5.00 m. Parallel parking instead takes 2.15 x 6.00 m: narrower, but longer to allow the manoeuvre.

q: In continental seating, what spacing applies to a row of up to 45 seats?
n: 525 mm, between the 500 mm allowed to 35 seats and the 550 mm required beyond 46.

q: Which housing type gets pooled parking at one slot per 10 units?
n: Low-income single-detached units on 100 sq m lots.

q: Under PD 1096, what parking slot size serves an articulated truck?
n: 3.60 x 18.00 m, the largest slot in the Code.

q: What is the maximum seat width in continental seating?
n: 480 mm maximum, 450 mm minimum.

q: Under RA 9514, what width must an aisle have when it serves seats on both sides?
n: 1220 mm both sides, against PD 1096 which asks 1.00 m.

q: Under PD 957, what parking slot size applies to parallel parking in open market housing?
n: 2.00 x 6.00 m: longer than a perpendicular slot, because a car must swing in from the lane.

q: What row spacing applies to chair seating?
n: 850 mm for loose chairs, slightly more than the 840 mm used for fixed seats.

q: Under PD 1096, how many seats may sit between a wall and an aisle, and between two aisles?
n: 7 against a wall, 14 between aisles, rising to 30 where doors run along each side.

q: Under PD 1096, how far from the building may off-site parking be?
n: Up to 200 m. BP 220 allows only 100 m, since socialized housing residents are likelier to walk.

q: Under RA 9514, what is the minimum row spacing in a seating area?
n: 680 mm minimum, 830 mm maximum.

q: Where poles stand less than 50 m apart, which poles carry street lighting?
n: Every other pole.

q: Under PD 1096, what parking ratio applies to a residential unit on a lot below 50 sq m?
n: One slot per 8 units. Smaller lots pool more heavily.

q: How many seats may normally sit between two aisles?
n: 14 between aisles, against 7 where one end is a wall.

q: Which drainage solution is specified with a load-bearing cover?
n: A concrete-lined canal, used in economic and socialized housing so the cover can take a vehicle.

q: Under BP 220, what parking ratio applies to economic or socialized housing on lots above 100 sq m?
n: One slot per 20 units, far thinner than the one slot per unit PD 1096 asks on comparable lots.

q: How many seats may sit between aisles within a building where seats have no backrest?
n: 6. Add a backrest indoors and the row can grow; take it outdoors without one and it reaches 15.

q: Which law sets the standards for economic and socialized housing?
n: BP 220. PD 957 covers the open market and medium cost tiers above it.

q: What minimum width must a side aisle have in a seating area?
n: 1.10 m, the same figure PD 1096 uses for a corridor.

q: How is the required water tank capacity sized?
n: 20% of average daily demand plus a fire reserve.

q: Which law is the Fire Code of the Philippines in force today?
n: RA 9514 of 2008, which repealed PD 1185 of 1977.

q: What width must each pair of exit doors have in a seating area?
n: 1.70 m per pair, one pair for every 5 rows.

q: In open market and medium cost housing, what septic tank arrangement is required?
n: An individual tank per unit, per PD 856. Only economic and socialized housing may go communal.

q: Under PD 1096, what clear spacing separates the back of one seat row from the front of the next?
n: 300 mm of clear space, within a total 840 mm back-to-back pitch.

q: Under RA 9514, what is the maximum slope of a seating aisle?
n: 12.5%, the same 1:8 PD 1096 allows.

q: What is a 300 mm drainage pipe in centimetres?
n: 30 cm. It is the minimum diameter PD 957 allows.

q: What does LCPD stand for in a water demand figure?
n: Litres per capita per day. Subdivision housing is designed at 150 LCPD.

q: Under RA 9514, what aisle width serves seats on both sides?
n: 1220 mm. PD 1096 is more lenient at 1.00 m.

q: What minimum drainage system is required for economic and socialized housing?
n: A concrete-lined canal with a load-bearing cover, a cheaper option than the concrete pipes required above that tier.

q: What is PD 856?
n: The Sanitation Code of the Philippines, which governs septic tanks and water supply.

q: In continental seating, what spacing applies to a row of up to 18 seats?
n: 450 mm, the tightest band, because few people ever pass along that row.

q: Which vehicle uses a 3.60 x 12.00 m parking slot?
n: A standard truck or bus. A jeepney takes 3.00 x 9.00 m.

q: Under PD 1096, what parking slot size applies to parallel parking?
n: 2.15 x 6.00 m. It is narrower than the 2.50 m perpendicular slot but a metre longer.

q: In continental seating, what spacing applies to a row of 46 seats or more?
n: 550 mm, the widest band.

q: Under PD 1096, at what lot size does the parking ratio reach one slot per unit?
n: Above 100 sq m. Below that it pools: one per 4 units at 50 to 100 sq m, one per 8 under 50 sq m.

q: Under PD 1096, what parking slot size serves a jeepney or shuttle?
n: 3.00 x 9.00 m, between the 5.00 m car slot and the 12.00 m truck slot.

q: What row spacing applies to seats without a backrest?
n: 600 mm without a backrest, 750 mm with one.

q: Under PD 1096, what aisle widths apply when seats sit on one side and on both sides?
n: 800 mm for one side, 1.00 m for both. An aisle serving two rows carries twice the traffic.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what size must an accessible parking slot be?
n: 4.00 x 5.00 m. The 1994 IRR asked only 3.70 m wide; the 2024 revision widened it so a side transfer fits.

q: Under PD 1096, what back-to-front spacing separates successive seat rows?
n: 300 mm clear between the back of one row and the front of the next.

q: What lets the number of seats between aisles rise from 14 to 30?
o: Doors are provided along each side
The aisle is widened to 2 m
The seats are fixed to the wall
n: Doors running along each side, so occupants leave sideways instead of walking the whole row.

q: Under BP 220, how far from the building may off-site parking be?
n: Up to 100 m, half the 200 m PD 1096 allows.

q: Under RA 9514, what back-to-front spacing separates successive seat rows?
n: 300 mm, the same clearance PD 1096 requires.

q: Which law governs septic tank requirements in a subdivision?
n: PD 856, the Sanitation Code of the Philippines.

q: Under PD 1096, what parking ratio applies to a residential unit on a lot of 50 to 100 sq m?
n: One slot per 4 units, between one per 8 below 50 sq m and one per unit above 100 sq m.

q: With doors along each side, how many seats may sit between aisles?
n: Up to 30, against the normal 14, because each row has its own way out.

q: Who may collect garbage in a subdivision?
n: The local government unit, or the subdivision independently.

q: Under PD 1096, what width must an aisle have when it serves seats on one side only?
n: 800 mm, rising to 1.00 m where seats flank both sides.

q: How many seats may sit between aisles in open-air seating with a backrest?
n: 6, the same as indoor seating without a backrest.
